spans.text: Morning.
The Gray Institute of Biotechnology.
Mrs. Gray peels off her plastic gloves and washes her hands at the washing basin.
Your test results look pretty decent this time as well.
You can get off the strict diet for now.
But no cigarettes or alcohol for you.
Thank you, Mrs. Gray.
Sorry for taking up your time.
Not at all. You are very welcome.
By the way, I hear the launch of Idunn has been giving you quite the trouble.
Gray smiles faintly. She places her index finger against her lips and shakes her head.
Forgive me, but I don't talk about business in my clinic.
Here, I'm just a simple doctor.
...I see.
Do excuse me. In that case, we'll discuss this some other time.
The man smiles apologetically at Gray and leaves a card of a restaurant.
If you don't mind, how about over some dinner?
It would be my pleasure.
Gray accepts the card courteously and gives a nod.
The man smiles in satisfaction and turns to leave.
Just as the man is about to walk out the door, he finds himself face-to-face with a ferocious-looking woman who appeared out of nowhere.
The woman glares past him straight at Gray. The coldness in her eyes sends chills running down his spine.
Who...Who are you? Who let you in?!
...Scram while you can.
This has nothing to do with you.
Pardon?!
Mr. Falk.
The man is just about to lose his temper over Ange's impudence when Gray speaks up softly from behind.
She is my guest.
Y-Your guest?!
He looks at the impeccably dressed Gray and back at Ange, who looks like a beggar in her tattered clothes, and gapes in disbelief.
Unbelievable! Why would you be associated with such low-life?!
Not to mention she's obviously here to make trouble!
Hm...
Gray smiles.
I do believe you are right... After all, we had a bit of a disagreement last night.
L-Last night?!
...We have a date.
Ange fishes out a name card from her waist pouch.
The color isn't particularly eye-catching, but everyone present can instantly recognize that it is indeed Gray's card.
...As you can see, Mr. Falk.
Would you mind giving us ladies some privacy?
Ange enters the room silently, holding the door open for the man.
Still incredulous, the man swallows and stalks out of the room.
The door shuts, leaving the two women alone inside.
I've seen that man before.
If memory serves, he's from Drug Administration, isn't he?
Mr. Falk is one of my patients and a regular.
He comes to me for medical check-ups regularly.
Gray tears up the fancy-looking card carelessly and tosses the scraps into the garbage can. She dusts off her hands and walks up to the washing basin again.
Ange watches her leisurely movements and for a moment is almost fooled by this woman's nonchalance.
"We had a disagreement last night"?
What a roundabout way of putting it.
A doctor needs to be tactful when informing patients about their condition.
After rubbing every nook and cranny on her hands clean, Gray dries her hands with a towel and takes out a pair of gray gloves.
I thought a doctor's job is to give their patients all the facts.
But a doctor can nevertheless be tactful about it. It's merely the compassionate thing to do.
Gray fiddles a little with the elastic edge of her glove and turns around. She gestures at the operating table in the center of the room.
Lie down.
...Lie down where?
Only two kinds of people would enter an operating room—doctors and patients.
I'm the doctor, so you're the patient.
Gray adjusts the height of the table and prepares the robotic arms.
She looks at Ange and invites her to lie down again.
Your prosthetics are about to give out.
Lie down, Angelia.
Her tone makes it obvious that she's not taking no for an answer.
Ange slowly approaches the operating table—and Gray.
You don't seem at all surprised to see me here.
I could blow your brains out right now and be done with it.
You won't, because you know that my death will change nothing.
Gray shrugs. Ange snickers and studies the room while leaning against the table.
Don't you need nurses?
My nurses don't tend to enter the operating room.
Let me guess—they're busy committing murder and arson at your bidding at night?
Ange walks up to Gray with her pistol tilted up ever so slightly.
You were right though...
My prosthetics are getting rickety. Could you please fix me up, Doc?
I'd be happy to.
The two women, very different in height, exchange disquieting smiles. Ange's finger is poised on her trigger.
Gray's gaze strays from Ange's face to her hand.
Are you bringing that to the operating table?
Agents are always a little paranoid.
Ange hasn't lifted her pistol, but Gray can tell with just a glance that the safety is off.
Unfortunately, I'm a surgeon, not a psychiatrist.
I'm afraid I can't do anything about your PTSD—unless you like my radical treatment.
Thanks, but no thanks.
Also, there's no telling if you're just a psycho in a white coat.
Maybe I'm actually your psychiatrist.
What an amusing thought.
I like psychiatrists. I also like psychological tests.
Have you heard of the Rorschach inkblot test?
Yes, what about it?
That's the first psychological test I've taken.
My teacher administered it on me.
You had teachers?
Didn't you?
Ange never looks away from Gray. After a while, she slides onto the operating table and lies down slowly.
Her pistol is still in her hand, but she has placed her bionic arm on the arm support.
Gray puts on a loupe and picks out several tools that Ange has never seen from her shelf.
What's your plan, Angelia?
Plan?
You've been scrutinizing my operating room ever since you walked through the door...
Then you started chatting away with me like an old friend. To be honest, when you said you could shoot me, I actually expected you to do it then and there.
But now, here you are, lying in front of me with nothing but a pistol.
Gray looks down at Ange's face tenderly.
Like a fish on a chopping block.
I know you're bold, but I didn't expect you to go so far.
So are you going to kill me now?
You won't get a better chance than this. I'm lying just inches away from you.
You just have to slit my throat with that scalpel and I will cease being a nuisance.
We're both gambling with very high stakes.
Well? Are you making a move or not?
...I'm a doctor, Angelia. I will never turn a patient on my operating table into a corpse.
Gray caresses Ange's bionic arm and smiles faintly.
Now tell me, what new cards have you got?
Berlin Prison. Quarantine wall. Bohnsdorf. Underground tunnel.
Altes Stadthaus. Marshallstraße. The Fernsehturm.
Ange recites a list of seemingly unrelated places.
Gray's hands freeze for just a fraction of a second.
You've been plotting and staging a series of minor incidents and terrorist attacks in Berlin since a few months ago.
Now the entire city is shrouded in a sense of dread and unrest, and you're obviously fanning the fire.
Ange studies Gray's perfectly smooth and nonplussed expression. She was hoping this woman would at least look a tiny bit surprised.
I knew you wouldn't let go of this piece of straw that you've grasped.
I have genuine admiration for Leone. Her talent is truly unparalleled.
After injecting coolant into the bionic arm interface, Gray disconnects the synaptic transmission.
Ange feels a sense of emptiness where her arm is missing—a sensation she hasn't experienced in a while.
She involuntarily tightens her grip on her pistol. For a second, she is certain Gray is going to strike.
But Gray shows no sign of wanting to attack. She simply carries on taking apart the joint of Ange's bionic arm with the help of some intricate device.
But the intention of orchestrating such attacks isn't to inflict casualties, but to sow chaos.
Besides, your plans are a lot more elaborate than most actual terrorist attacks.
Berlin isn't your target. You're going for the top brass.
Gray rotates the lens on her loupe. A spark flares from one of Ange's bionic finger joints.
And so you've come to me.
You know you can't influence the situation on your own.
Your only solution is to find an opening through me.
Is that why you'd risk your own life to extract the information you're after from me?
Through her loupe, Gray eyes Ange with admiration.
You really are an exceptional agent, Angelia.
People like you shine brightly wherever you go.
This must be why the Soviets are using you as a cat's paw.
So you admit you ARE going for them?
Have you never considered a change of clothing, Angelia?
You've never wanted anything to do with the power-hungry and opportunistic old nobility... Don't play dumb. I know how much you hate those who make nothing but empty promises.
With your talent, you can achieve so much more—just think about it.
Would you rather do something great in a brave new world or toil away for some dwindling flame in the old world?
...You're an eloquent speaker.
Sadly, I'm not interested at all.
I fight only for myself.
...That's a real shame.
Gray looks up. The final calibration is complete as she wraps up her rousing speech.
She reconnects Ange's synaptic transmission, and Ange regains her sense of touch on the bionic arm.
Ange curls her hand into a fist and can immediately tell how much more crisp and responsive her arm feels after the maintenance.
She is mildly taken aback.
I can see why you're so well respected.
In this day and age, a doctor who is this accomplished in both medicine and prosthetic engineering...
...is highly coveted everywhere.
But doctors alone can't cure the world.
The people need a dose of strong medicine.
What you're doing will only inflict more pain and suffering on the world.
I may not share those old farts' vision, but you stand for everything that I'm against.
You and your brothers and sisters are cancer to this world.
Your so-called "strong medicine" is without a doubt strong poison.
Ange sits up with her gun pointed straight at Gray's face.
Was it your "teacher" who put such twisted ideas in your head?
Gray eyes Ange's pistol and shakes her head.
...My teacher has simply helped me find my true self.
No one can determine who you are—surely you know that better than I do.
Still, my teacher holds you in extremely high regard, which is why you caught my eye to begin with.
Your teacher knows me? Who is your teacher?
You've spent such a wonderful time in each other's company.
She looks back at those days with great fondness...and she can't wait to see you again.
Still, she did say if you get in my way, I don't have to worry about sparing her feelings.
...Your teacher is...Morridow?
Hush...
Resting her chin on one hand, Gray brushes a fingertip gently along Ange's bionic arm and observes the change in Ange's expression with great interest.
The hand with which Ange is holding her pistol suddenly goes limp. The heavy pistol slips out from her grip and clatters on the floor.
Don't say her name.
Right now, I'm your dance partner.
What...did you do to my body?
Anesthetics. It's necessary for surgery.
Just doing my job as a doctor.
Gray reaches out and picks up the gun that's lying on the floor. She dangles it in front of Ange's face.
Leone really is a genius, don't you think?
I have never met anyone else with such a profound understanding of botany.
Ugh...!
Ange grits her teeth, but her paralyzed body refuses to obey her. She ends up rolling off the operating table.
If she hadn't made such a regrettable decision, I'm sure we would have been great friends.
Gray lets out a sigh. Still holding Ange's pistol, she walks around to the other side of the operating table and points the gun at Ange, who's lying on the floor, immobilized.
The same goes for you, Angelia.
If you had given me a different answer, it wouldn't have come to this.
You...!
You...You're also...a Nyto!
Correct. I confess, I'm quite surprised.
You did not suspect me at all even after what happened with Morridow. This is entirely unlike you.
...The Lady of Ashes is a legendary prodigy in the medical field and has been renowned for over ten years.
Your background is spotless... Unless you've been setting the stage since ten years ago.
Otherwise, this can't possibly...
That is indeed something that's easily overlooked.
Gray nods in acknowledgment.
Ange flips herself over with great difficulty. As she stares at Gray's ageless face, she is suddenly struck by a terrible realization.
...Gray is dead, isn't she?
You...You took her place.
How many are there?
I know you can't be the only one... How many Nytos have infiltrated human society?!
You ask too many questions, Angelia.
But count yourself lucky. I will not kill you just yet; we are quite interested in some of the information that you have.
Gray shrugs and bends down to Ange's eye level, as if she's fawning over a child.
Ange starts gasping for breath. Gray watches her and smiles gleefully.
You're too arrogant, Angelia.
Why have you come alone?
Heh...
Ange looks back at Gray and suddenly lets out a chuckle.
What's so funny?
...It's hilarious...
You really are Morridow's pupil.
You even...make the exact same mistake.
Gray's face blanches instantly—
Boom!
The wall of Gray's clinic is blown apart.
Bang!
A single round flies through the billowing dust and knocks the pistol right out of Gray's hand before she can react.
Tsk!
The pistol clatters onto the floor.
When she looks back again, Ange has already dragged her paralyzed body away from her.
Target locked on. Be careful, Ange is in close proximity!
Subduing the target.
AK-15 raises her rifle again and pulls the trigger.
A metallic clang rings out.
Something has darted out from behind Gray and blocked the bullet.
It is a long and slender metal tendril with a sharp blade at the tip.
It looks like a scorpion's tail.
In the face of the menacing Dolls, Gray has no intention of getting into a fight. With a single leap, she reaches the wall in the back.
She shoots one last threatening look at Ange before finally turning away.
Then her powerful tail smashes the glass over an emergency button. Before AK-15 can stop her, the wall behind Gray suddenly swivels, and Gray disappears without a trace.
Crap, a trap door!
It's built with a special material. I can't find it!
The alarm goes off and heavy metal gates come slamming down on all four walls of the operating room.
Ange, we need to retreat!
We won't make it if we don't go now!
Dammit!
With AK-15's help, Ange scrambles back to her feet.
Quick, we're going back!
Where?
Ange growls through gritted teeth.
The sanatorium!
I bet...she's headed straight to Leone!
